summary: EmailPopupDocument manages email-related document records, supporting search, retrieval, and deletion of email file data. It handles parsing structured input, maintains document metadata, and safely deletes files and folders associated with emails.
purpose: To provide structured handling of email document files—including listing, metadata storage, and deletion of both files and directories—by parsing a delimited input string and performing file system operations.

fields.name: FileName
fields.description: Name of the email document file

fields.name: FilePath
fields.description: Full system path to the document file

fields.name: Checked
fields.description: Indicates if the document is checked

workflows.name: Search Email Documents
steps: Split DataInfo on '|' to get email record segments.
For each segment: Split by '>' to parse FileName and FilePath.
Instantiate EmailPopupDocument for each valid segment.
Add each document entry to the result list.

workflows.name: Delete Email Document
steps: Receive DataInfo and target ID as input.
Split DataInfo on '|' to get email record segments.
Iterate over segments to find the one matching the provided ID.
If found, split by '>' to get FilePath.
Attempt to delete the file at FilePath.
Attempt to delete the containing folder.
For non-deleted records, concatenate back into the output string.

business_rules: EmailPopupDocument only processes entries with two parts (FileName and FilePath) split by '>'.
Only the entry matching the provided ID in the Delete workflow is deleted; others are preserved.
Exceptions during file or folder deletion are caught and do not interrupt the workflow.
validations: DataInfo must not be null or empty.
Email record segments must split into exactly two parts ('>' delimiter) for valid processing.
calculations: ID is incremented for each entry during search workflow.
conditions: If DataInfo is empty, workflows return empty results.
If emailData length is not 2, entry is skipped.
system_behavior: System performs file and directory deletions when deleting an email document.
System catches and ignores exceptions during file or directory deleting operations.
dependencies: System.IO for file and directory manipulation.
Delimited input string format ('|' and '>') for workflow logic.
exceptions: File deletion or directory deletion may throw exceptions, which are caught and ignored.
content_gaps: No information on how DataInfo input is constructed or managed outside of these workflows.
No authentication or authorization logic mentioned.
No information on Checked field usage beyond storage.
